relevance_reason: Identifies homozygous C15ORF41 mutations as a cause of CDAN1-negative congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I, which defines CDA type Ib.

findings.statement: In a consanguineous family of Middle Eastern origin with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I, Babbs et al. (2013) used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to identify a homozygous c.533T>A transversion in the C15ORF41 gene, which was predicted to result in a p.L178Q substitution. No likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation had been found in this family.
quotes: We used whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis to identify a homozygous T to A transversion (c.533T>A), predicted to lead to a p.L178Q missense substitution in C15ORF41, a gene of unknown function, in a consanguineous pedigree of Middle-Eastern origin.

findings.statement: By sequencing C15ORF41 in other congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I families without CDAN1 mutations, Babbs et al. (2013) found a homozygous c.281A>G transition, predicted to result in a p.Y94C substitution, in 2 more families of Southeast Asian origin.
quotes: Sequencing C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I pedigrees identified a homozygous transition (c.281A>G), predicted to lead to a p.Y94C substitution, in two further pedigrees of SouthEast Asian origin.

findings.statement: Babbs et al. (2013) reported that the haplotype around the c.281A>G mutation in C15ORF41 suggested a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan.
quotes: The haplotype surrounding the c.281A>G change suggests a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan.

findings.statement: Babbs et al. (2013) noted that CDAN1 mutations underlie most cases of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. However, no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation is found in about 20% of cases, which suggested that at least one other locus exists.
quotes: Mutations in the CDAN1 gene, which encodes Codanin-1, underlie the majority of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I cases. However, no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation has been detected in approximately 20% of cases, suggesting the presence of at least one other locus.

findings.statement: Using detailed sequence similarity searches, Babbs et al. (2013) predicted that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease belonging to the Holliday junction resolvase protein family.
quotes: Detailed sequence similarity searches indicate that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease that is a member of the Holliday junction resolvase family of proteins.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports that linkage and mutation analysis of CDAN1 showed genetic heterogeneity in CDA type I, which supports a separate, non-CDAN1 form (CDA Ib).

findings.statement: Ahmed et al. (2006) performed linkage and mutation analysis of the CDAN1 gene in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I and found genetic heterogeneity.
quotes: Linkage and mutational analysis of the CDAN1 gene reveals genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports evidence of genetic heterogeneity in CDA type I, which is the basis for distinguishing a type Ib form.

findings.statement: Ahmed et al. (2006) reported evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
quotes: Evidence of genetic heterogeneity in congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type I.

relevance_reason: The paper describes three Bedouin sibs with CDA type 1 who also had distal limb anomalies and other dysmorphic features. This is the clinical picture that sets CDA type Ib apart.

findings.statement: Sabry et al. (1997) described 3 Bedouin sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I who also had dysmorphic features. These included growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail and phalangeal hypoplasia of fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of toes, and hallux valgus. The phenotype varied among the sibs.
quotes: Dysmorphic features in three sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type 1 are described.

These findings include growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail/phalangeal hypoplasia of fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of toes, and hallux valgus.
Phenotypic heterogeneity was elicited amongst the three Bedouin sibs.

phenotypes.text: nail hypoplasia of fingers and toes

findings.statement: Sabry et al. (1997) found a very low mitotic index in peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures from the 3 affected sibs. They suggested that a low mitotic index and congenital ptosis could be part of the syndrome.
quotes: The patients also showed a very low mitotic index of their peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures.
suggests that other traits, congenital ptosis and low mitotic index, could represent part of the syndrome profile.

phenotypes.text: very low mitotic index of peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures

findings.statement: Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed an association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I and a specific form of distal limb anomalies. This suggested a distinct entity.
quotes: The present report confirms the association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia type 1 and a specific form of distal limb anomalies
